Repo: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa — branch `feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui`, currently at 542ac65.

READ-ONLY TASK. Do not edit, write, stage, commit, or run any git state-changing command. Two other agent sessions are live in this same working tree — do not mutate anything. Use `git show`, `git diff`, `git log`, and file reads only. You may RUN `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` since it is a read-only audit script, and report what it outputs.

CONTEXT: Tim Lavelle made 13 commits (range `ec9d161..542ac65`). The reader is the project's Frontend Development Lead and knows this area deeply — they personally discovered and documented two traps in this codebase:

(a) The Zimmermann spacing scale is registered ONLY as `theme.space`. A bare token key like `spacing="m"` works, but the same bare key on a SIZING prop (`width`, `height`, `boxSize`, `minWidth`, `maxHeight`) falls through to Chakra's own `sizes` scale and silently misresolves — measured 8x to 112x wrong, and keys `s`/`m`/`l` are absent entirely so those declarations are dropped.
(b) `theme.fontSizes`, `theme.lineHeights` and `theme.letterSpacings` were never registered at all, so `fontSize="2xs"` resolves to Chakra's default rather than the Zimmermann value, and `fontSize="l"` emits nothing. There is a known live instance at `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx:302`.

The reader also documented a rule that `var(--zimm-*)` CSS variables belong in theme recipes, never in component JSX. Tim's commits appear to have formalised policy in exactly this area, so determine whether Tim's changes SOLVE these traps, ENCODE them as policy, or WORK AROUND them.

YOUR DOMAIN: theme and token policy. Two commits:
- `9d5f89c` refactor(theme): require var(--zimm-*) over bare Chakra token keys in overrides
- `466e62b` feat(theme): build scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs, close the missing-audit gap

Note `overrides/app/theme/foundation/` is Tier 1 (frozen, UI-designer-owned); `overrides/app/theme/components/` and `globalStyles.ts` are Tier 2.

GOAL IS COMPREHENSION, NOT AUDIT of the codebase. Deliver an explanation of what Tim changed and what it means. Not a findings list.

Investigate and explain:
1. The new policy in `9d5f89c`. What exactly is now required, where is it written down, and what is the stated rationale? Quote it.
2. Does the policy actually fix trap (a) and trap (b) above, or does it sidestep them by mandating `var(--zimm-*)` everywhere so the broken Chakra scale lookup never happens? Be precise — this distinction matters enormously to the reader. If it is a workaround rather than a fix, say so and explain what remains broken underneath.
3. Were any foundation files touched (Tier 1)? If so, which, and were scales newly registered in `theme/index.ts`? Check specifically whether `fontSizes`/`lineHeights`/`letterSpacings`/`sizes` are now registered.
4. `scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` — read it thoroughly and explain: what does it detect, how (regex? AST?), what does it deliberately NOT detect, what are its false-positive/false-negative characteristics, and is it wired into CI or a git hook or purely manual? Then RUN it and report the actual current output.
5. Does the audit script catch the two traps above? Specifically, would it flag `fontSize="l"` at `header/index.tsx:302`, or a bare spacing key on a `width` prop? Test your claim against the real file rather than assuming.
6. What a developer must now do differently when styling a component. Give a concrete correct example and a concrete now-wrong example, from real code.
7. Anything surprising, or where the new policy conflicts with `.claude/rules/css.md` / `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` as they currently read.

Report in clear prose with file:line citations and short excerpts. Be exhaustive within this domain — the reader knows this area well, so precision matters more than breadth of caveats.

Chakra UI and `.scss` conventions. See [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) > Rules > Styling for the
higher-level policy (Chakra props first, `.scss` only when insufficient, theme file
ownership/tiers) — this file covers the concrete day-to-day rules underneath that policy.

Chakra UI props must use the Chakra token system — no hardcoded hex colours, no pixel
values for spacing, no raw font sizes. Tokens belong in
[overrides/app/theme/foundation/](../../overrides/app/theme/) (Tier 1 — see
[frozenFiles.md](./frozenFiles.md)).

```tsx
// ❌ hardcoded
<Box color="#1A1A1A" padding="16px" />

// ❌ a bare Chakra/theme token string — resolves correctly (theme.colors/theme.space ARE
// registered from the Zimmermann foundations) but is still not allowed in an override

<Box color="text.default" padding="m" />

// ✅ token, as a raw var(--zimm-*) reference

```

a raw `fontSize`, per [overrideStyling.md](./overrideStyling.md) point 1. There's no

individual pieces (`var(--zimm-font-size-*)` etc.), so `textStyle` stays a bare key —

content.text:
## Summary

Tim's two theme commits do **not** touch trap (a) or trap (b). They add a third, orthogonal rule about *call-site legibility* for the scales that already work correctly, plus a long-promised hex/px audit script. Both traps remain exactly as you documented them, including the live instance at `header/index.tsx:302`, which I verified is still there and still unflagged by everything Tim built. There is one genuine, unadvertised improvement to trap detection buried in the commit — the 2^n prop-combination change — which I'll come to.

---

## 1. The new policy in `9d5f89c`

The policy is hierarchy point 2 of `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`, rewritten in place. It previously read "Semantic colour/spacing token strings — `color="text.default"`, `spacing="m"`". It now reads (`.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md:16-27`):

> 2. **Raw `var(--zimm-*)` CSS custom properties** for colour and spacing — `color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)"`, `bg="var(--zimm-color-bg-02)"`, `gap="var(--zimm-scale-m)"`. **Never** a bare Chakra/theme token string (`color="text.default"`, `gap="m"`) — even though `theme.colors`/`theme.space` ARE registered from the same Zimmermann foundations […] and a bare key resolves to the identical value. This is a house-style requirement, not a correctness one: a `var(--zimm-*)` reference is unambiguous at every call site, where a bare key forces a PR reviewer to check `theme/index.ts`'s registered-scale list to know whether it happens to be correct.

The commit message states the rationale identically: *"bare Chakra token keys and var(--zimm-\*) both resolve correctly today, but a bare key forces a PR reviewer to check theme/index.ts's registered-scale list to know whether it's actually correct — a raw zimm var is unambiguous at every call site regardless."*

Note the scope carefully: **colour and spacing only**. Typography is untouched and stays at point 1 (`textStyle`, never a raw `fontSize`). `css.md:29-32` explains why type is excluded — "There's no `var(--zimm-*)` substitute for the composite `textStyle` expansion itself, only for its individual pieces (`var(--zimm-font-size-*)` etc.), so `textStyle` stays a bare key — it's the one entry in the hierarchy that isn't a colour/spacing token." **Sizing props are not mentioned at all.**

It is written down in three places:
- `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md:16-27` — the normative statement.
- `.claude/rules/css.md:16-26` — the worked example, which now has *two* ❌ cases: the old hardcoded one, and a new one for `<Box color="text.default" padding="m" />`.
- `overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts:331-345` — a fifth guard, `'no override-component style uses a bare token key on a registered scale'`, filtering on a 34-entry `SPACE_PROPS` set (the full padding/margin/gap/inset family, including `top`/`left`/`right`/`bottom`) and an 8-entry `COLOR_PROPS` set, against `Object.keys(spacing)` and a recursively flattened `colors` key set.

The conversion is complete: 24 bare spacing keys and 5 bare colour tokens across 9 files, and my own grep for any surviving bare spacing key on a space prop across both scan roots returns nothing. The guard suite passes — I ran it, 6 tests green.

---

## 2. Fix or workaround? It is a workaround, and deliberately not a fix

Precisely: **neither trap is fixed, and neither is intended to be.** `theme/index.ts` is byte-identical — not just across these two commits but across all 13 in `ec9d161..542ac65` (`git log --name-only ec9d161..542ac65 -- overrides/app/theme/foundation/ overrides/app/theme/index.ts` returns empty). The registered set at `theme/index.ts:51-62` is still exactly `borderWidths, breakpoints, colors, fonts, space: spacing, textStyles`. `fontSizes`, `lineHeights`, `letterSpacings`, `sizes` and `transition` remain unregistered.

The important nuance is that the file's own comment (`theme/index.ts:31-39`) frames non-registration as permanent architecture, not debt:

> Deliberately NOT registered, because the Zimmermann scale and the Chakra scale use the same key names for different values — remapping them would silently restyle the base retail-react-app, which uses those names at ~199 call sites

So "fix" is not available as an option. Registering `fontSizes` *is* the breakage. Given that, the `var(--zimm-*)` mandate is the sanctioned mitigation, and it is a structurally effective one: `width: 'var(--zimm-scale-m)'` performs no `theme.sizes` lookup at all — Chakra passes the string through and the browser resolves the custom property — so the 8×–112× misresolution has no opportunity to occur. Likewise `fontSize: 'var(--zimm-font-size-2xs)'`, which `zimmTextInput.css.ts:112` already uses. Adherence makes trap-shaped mistakes impossible at the call sites that adhere.

But be clear about what that does and does not buy:

- **The policy does not cover the props where the traps live.** Point 2 says "colour and spacing". The new guard's `SPACE_PROPS` deliberately excludes `width`/`height`/`boxSize`/`minWidth`/`maxHeight`. So a bare spacing key on a sizing prop is not a violation of Tim's new rule at all — it is caught only by the **pre-existing** guard at `recipeGuards.test.ts:295` (`'no sizing property uses a bare spacing-scale key'`). Trap (b) likewise is caught only by the pre-existing guard at `:305`. Both of those came from `3ba238e` and `e686bd3`, which I confirmed are ancestors of `ec9d161` — i.e. they predate Tim's range and are not his work.
- **Tim's one real contribution to trap coverage is indirect but genuine.** He replaced `resolveBaseStyle` (one resolution, all booleans false) with `resolveAllBaseStyles`, which resolves a function-form `baseStyle` across all 2^5 = 32 combinations of `inverse`/`disabled`/`hasError`/`focused`/`filled`. Because `collect()` feeds *all* the value-level guards, the pre-existing trap (a) and trap (b) guards now walk conditional branches they previously never saw. The motivating case was `top: floated ? '3xs' : '50%'`, which shipped precisely because `floated` was false under the single default resolution. He verified this by reintroducing the bare value and confirming failure. So: the traps aren't fixed, but their in-recipe detection got materially deeper.
- **The JSX/`sx` blind spot is untouched and honestly documented.** `recipeGuards.test.ts:36-45`: "these guards walk the registered recipe map only […] They cannot see the same mistakes made as a JSX prop on a component — there is a live instance of failure mode 2 at `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx:302` (`fontSize="l"`, which emits nothing) that no test here can reach." I confirmed line 302 is unchanged: `<Text as="h2" fontSize="l" fontFamily="body" fontWeight="700">`. Tim extended that comment to note his own new guard shares the blind spot — `footerNavColumn/index.tsx` had a bare `paddingLeft: '2xs'` in an inline `sx` merge that "was only found by a manual grep […] not by this suite."
- **Incidentally, there is no `--zimm-font-size-l`.** The font-size vars are only `md`, `xs`, `2xs`, `3xs`, `4xs`. So `header:302` has no var-based remedy; the correct fix is `textStyle`, per point 1.

**And the policy introduces one new unchecked surface.** Making `var()` mandatory moves the token name from something with a key set behind it to an arbitrary string. Nothing validates that a referenced var exists. `theme/index.test.tsx:269-299` checks the *foundation → var* direction (every foundation constant has a `--zimm-*` twin); nothing checks *recipe reference → var exists*. The compound-shorthand guard actively treats var() as opaque: `f.value.replace(/var\([^)]*\)/g, 'VAR')` at `recipeGuards.test.ts:322`. So `var(--zimm-scale-mm)` or `var(--zimm-color-txt-default)` emits an unresolved custom property with no TS error and no test failure. I checked: 50 distinct vars are referenced across both scan roots and all 50 exist among the 125 defined in `zimmTokens.ts` — so this is latent exposure, not a live bug. But it is the cost side of the trade, and neither doc mentions it.

---

## 3. Tier 1

**No foundation file and no `theme/index.ts` were touched**, by either commit or by any commit in the range. No scale was newly registered. `fontSizes`/`lineHeights`/`letterSpacings`/`sizes` are all still absent from the `overrides` object.

However, two *other* Tier 1 surfaces were touched, which is worth flagging since the brief only asked about foundation:

- `.claude/rules/css.md` and `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` — `.claude/rules/` is Tier 1 Governance per `frozenFiles.md` (owner: both squad leads + Integration lead), routed at `CODEOWNERS:72` to `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`. Both commits modify it.
- `package.json` (root) — Tier 1 per `frozenFiles.md` "Runtime & Integration Config", `CODEOWNERS:53`. `466e62b` adds the `audit:tokens` script line.

So both commits require a tier-1 code-owner review before merge. Downstream derived AI configs (`.cursor/rules/tier2ProtectedFiles.mdc`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `.claude/registry/*.md`) were regenerated alongside, as the sync convention requires. One caveat: `npm run sync:ai-rules:check` currently reports `.github/copilot-instructions.md` as "source is 2 minutes newer" — that is a live-timestamp artefact of the other agent sessions mutating this tree right now, not attributable to Tim.

---

## 4. `scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`

**What it detects.** Raw hex colours and raw `px`/`rem`/`em` numeric literals. Exactly two regexes, `auditTokenUsage.mjs:57-58`:

```js
const HEX_RE = /#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}\b/g;
const UNIT_RE = /\b\d+(?:\.\d+)?(?:rem|em|px)\b/g;
```

**How.** Line-based regex, explicitly not AST. Self-documented at `:36-40`: *"This is a line-based grep, not an AST parse — matches `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`'s own framing ('it greps for exactly this')."* It does do one piece of real lexing: `stripComments` (`:83-104`) removes `//` and `/* */` content before matching, tracking block-comment state across lines, with a deliberate `line[i-1] !== ':'` guard at `:94` so a `'https://wa.me/…'` literal isn't truncated. So a Figma hex quoted in prose isn't a violation — but the acknowledgement check deliberately reads the *raw* lines (`:121`), so marker words in comments still register.

**Scope.** `SCAN_ROOTS` = `overrides/app/components` + `overrides/app/theme/components` (`:54`); `.ts`/`.tsx`/`.scss` (`:55`); excludes `*.test.ts(x)` and `*.stories.tsx` (`:61-62`).

**Acknowledged exceptions** (`:119-122`). Walk back from the match line to the nearest blank line or file start; test that contiguous block against `/provisional|pending|placeholder|audit-allow/i` (`:59`). A hit prints but does not affect the exit code. The commit message documents a real calibration story here: a fixed 2-line window missed cases where the marker word wrapped across a line break ("…52/40. Pending\n// Kiera."), hence the blank-line boundary.

**Wiring: purely manual.** `package.json:74` (`"audit:tokens": "node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs"`) is the *only* reference in the repo. I grepped `.github/`, `scripts/hooks/`, `.husky/`, `coderabbit.yaml` and `.coderabbit/` — nothing. Documented as intentional at `css.md:34-40`: "It's not wired into CI […] so nothing blocks a merge that skips running it — that's still a real gap, just not an unstarted one," and `overrideStyling.md` explains the precondition: someone must triage the pre-existing findings first.

**Deliberate non-detections** (`:11-17`): `foundation/` (raw values there "ARE the source of truth, so a raw value there is the point"), tests, stories.

**Undocumented blind spots, all provable from the real run:**
- **Non-hex colours are invisible.** `collectionHero.tsx:31` is `textShadow="0 1px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.4)"`. The run flags `'1px'` and `'4px'` and says nothing about `rgba(0,0,0,0.4)` — a hardcoded colour. `hsl()` and named colours likewise.
- **Units outside px/rem/em are invisible.** `header.ts:73` `width: 'min(597px, 60vw)'` → flags `'597px'`, not `'60vw'`. `:74` `'min(70px, 7.04vw)'` → flags `'70px'`, not `'7.04vw'`. `%`, `vw`, `vh`, `ch`, `pt` all pass.
- **Bare Chakra numerics pass.** `mb={4}` on that same `collectionHero.tsx:31` is not flagged; nor is `bg="gray.100"` at `productHero.tsx:46` — a non-Zimmermann Chakra colour.
- **Computed values pass.** `` `${n}px` `` has no literal digits.
- **Two styling surfaces are out of scope entirely.** `overrides/app/theme/globalStyles.ts` (Tier 2, ships CSS on every page — 8 lines match the regexes) and `overrides/app/pages/**` (3 files match: `experience/index.tsx`, `home/index.tsx`, `my-new-route/index.tsx`).

**False-negative channels in the allow-list mechanism:**
- **No word boundaries on the marker regex.** I tested it: `"depending on the viewport"` **matches**, `"appending a suffix"` **matches**. So an innocuous comment containing "depending" silences every raw literal in its contiguous block. Currently latent — the two live `independent` instances correctly don't match — but it is a live-fire hazard the moment someone writes "depending on the breakpoint" above a px value.
- **Block-scope, not line-scope.** One marker anywhere above, within an unbroken run of non-blank lines, acknowledges everything below it in that run.
- **The escape hatch is prose, self-service and unreviewed.** `466e62b`'s own fix for `zimmButton.css.ts` was to *reword a comment* — adding "PROVISIONAL" and "pending sign-off" — while `BTN_HEIGHT_LG`/`SM`/`PADDING_Y` stayed `'50px'`/`'41px'`/`'5px'`. Legitimate here (it's the documented Handover conflict), but it demonstrates that the gate is satisfied by editing prose rather than a value.

## 7. Surprises and live conflicts

**(a) `overrideStyling.md` now contradicts itself, and the contradiction is load-bearing.** The "Component-local tokens" section (`.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md:135-146`) was not touched by either commit and still says:

> When a component needs a spacing/sizing value that already has a `spacing.ts` / `iconSizes` / etc. entry, reference it **by name** in the theme config (`marginBottom: 'xs'`, not `marginBottom: 2` or `marginBottom: '0.5rem'`) — Chakra resolves named scale keys against the registered `theme.space` automatically.

`marginBottom` is in the new guard's `SPACE_PROPS` and `'xs'` is in `SPACING_KEYS`, so **following that paragraph literally now fails `npm run test`.** It goes on to endorse the responsive form `['2xs', '2xs', 'xs', 'xs']`, which the guard also walks (per `e686bd3`, "see responsive forms"). And it cites `theme/components/imageGallery.ts` / `swatchGroup.ts` as the exemplars of the pattern — **neither file exists**; `theme/components/` now contains only `footerShared.ts`, `header.ts`, `index.ts`, `listMenu.ts`, `navConstants.ts`, `recipeGuards.test.ts`. So 120 lines below the new mandate, the same file recommends the forbidden pattern and points at two deleted files as proof. This is the one thing I'd fix first.

**(b) `css.md` reads contradictorily on a skim.** `css.md:11` still opens the section with "Chakra UI props must use the Chakra token system", five lines above an example marking a Chakra token string as ❌. Both statements are defensible in context, but the section heading and its example now pull in opposite directions.

**(c) The policy direction is an inversion worth naming.** The mandate pushes styling *out* of Chakra's token system and into raw CSS custom properties — and per `theme/index.ts:21-24`, `--zimm-*` vars are injected by a raw `<Global>` in `_app-config/index.tsx`, deliberately bypassing Chakra's style processor. So the newly-mandatory surface is the one Chakra doesn't resolve. That is precisely what makes it immune to the registered-scale question, and precisely what removes any name-level checking (see §2's dangling-var point). The rationale as written is entirely about reviewer legibility; the type-safety cost isn't acknowledged in either doc.

**(d) Enforcement is asymmetric in an unusual way.** The *house-style* rule — explicitly "not a correctness one" — is mechanically gated on every test run. The *correctness* rules (traps a and b in JSX) and the raw-literal audit are not gated at all. The strongest enforcement sits on the weakest-stakes rule.

**(e) `header.ts`'s two `min()` expressions are a genuine blocker to CI wiring**, not just triage backlog. `width: 'min(597px, 60vw)'` is deliberate fluid sizing with no token form, and the audit can only ever see the `px` half of it. Someone will have to `audit-allow` those two before `audit:tokens` can become a required check, which slightly undercuts the "just needs triage" framing in the docs.
